title: Length of a module
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ an $R$-module. The length $\mathrm{length}_R(M)\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ is the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain of $R$-submodules $0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_n=M$ with $M_{i-1}\ne M_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. Equivalently, it is the supremum of the numbers $n$ of proper inclusions in all strict chains $N_0\subsetneq N_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq N_n$ of $R$-submodules of $M$ (a strict chain not starting at $0$ or not ending at $M$ is lengthened by adding $0$ below or $M$ on top, so the two suprema agree). $M$ has *finite length* if $\mathrm{length}_R(M)<\infty$.
